subject: Draft MAP & acceptance timeline for OmniCorp pilot
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@omnicorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP & acceptance timeline for OmniCorp pilot

Hi Carlos —

Thanks again for the time today. I promised to share a lightweight mutual action plan (MAP) so your engineering and product teams can validate timelines and success criteria quickly. I attached a short MAP template (Google Doc) and a one-tab metrics workbook with suggested signals we typically use for pilot acceptance.

Key asks:
- Can you confirm the two evaluation tracks we discussed (latency/cost and quality/regression)?
- Please flag any legal/security gating items early — we can loop in our security lead if needed.
- Review the proposed week-by-week milestones in the doc and comment by EOD Tuesday if possible.

Proposed high-level timeline (draft):
1) Week 0: access + test dataset ingestion
2) Week 1–2: integration + baseline runs
3) Week 3: iterative tuning + quantization trial
4) Week 4: acceptance window + sign-off

I attached: MAP-template-v1.gdoc (link included below) and pilot-acceptance-metrics.xlsx. I will convert the doc to a co-edit link so your team can annotate.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_MAP_TEMPLATE
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/OMNI-4761

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP-template-v1.gdoc (gdoc), pilot-acceptance-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@omnicorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & acceptance timeline for OmniCorp pilot

Stephanie —

Appreciate the draft. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Data retention / logs — our security team will want to confirm retention windows and whether inference logs are exportable for audit.
2) Quality metrics — can you add an example of the quality baseline metric (e.g., simulated user prompts + expected pass rate)?
3) Timeline — Week 4 feels tight for full acceptance given our internal review cadence. Can we build a flexible window: accept window opens in week 4 and runs through week 6?

If you can add those items to the doc I will share internally and get back with availability for a joint review.

—Carlos
Carlos Ramirez | Head of Product Integrations, OmniCorp
c.ramirez@omnicorp.com

Hi Carlos —

Thanks for the quick feedback. I updated the MAP doc with two edits: a short section (under Acceptance Criteria -> Security) explaining our default retention and export options, and an example quality baseline (sample prompt set + pass-rate threshold). I also expanded the timeline to give you an acceptance window from Week 4 through Week 6 and added a soft "pause" task for procurement gating.

Quick notes on items you asked about:
- Retention: default 30 days for debug logs; retention policy configurable via our Private offering; we can provide an export (jsonl) for audit.
- Quality baseline: added example (see sheet "QualityExample") — we typically run 500 synthetic prompts and validate a >= 85% pass rate for the first acceptance tranche.
- Procurement: added a row for PO + SSO + IP addendum sign-off (owner: OmniCorp Legal).

Link (co-edit): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_MAP_TEMPLATE
I attached the workbook as well to this thread for your records.

If that looks ok I can schedule a 30-min review with engineering next Tue morning — does 10:00 AM PT work for you?

—Marissa Cole
Principal Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: pilot-acceptance-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet)
